name: Western Australia
summary_text: WA's Equal Opportunity Act 1984 protects the attribute of "gender history," defined as a person who "identifies as a member of the opposite sex by living, or seeking to live, as a member of the opposite sex." This is a narrower, medically-inflected, binary formulation than the "gender identity" language used in Victoria, Queensland and the federal Sex Discrimination Act. A non-binary or gender-nonconforming visitor may not meet the state-law definition and would rely solely on federal coverage for a state-level complaint. WA has no state anti-vilification offence (civil or criminal) and no statutory charter of rights binding public authorities. Reform is underway: the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Amendment (Sex or Gender Changes) Act 2024 received assent on 26 September 2024, removing medical and surgical prerequisites for registration of a sex or gender change, with substantive commencement by proclamation. This feeds back into the scope of "gender history" for complaints purposes but is not yet fully in force as of the scoring date. Vs the national score of 0.86, WA sits 0.02 below: the narrower protective vocabulary and absence of both a vilification offence and a rights charter mean the state-level safety net is thinner than in eastern states, even though the federal floor is unchanged. Vs Queensland (national, no deviation record), which has a Human Rights Act 2019 binding public authorities and a conversion-practice prohibition in force since 2020, WA lacks both structural review and the specific coercion safeguard.

sources.claim_summary: NOTE: consolidated PDF of the Equal Opportunity Act 1984 (WA) was not retrievable at fetch time (state legislation portal blocks automated fetches); the companion official explainer below quotes the operative definitions - the Act protects the attribute 'gender history', defined by living, or seeking to live, as a member of the opposite sex, with complaint eligibility tied to recognition certificates or registry change under the Births, Deaths and Marriages framework.

sources.title: Gender History Discrimination Information
sources.claim_summary: WA government public 'Gender History Discrimination Information' page: unlawful to discriminate because of gender history under the Equal Opportunity Act 1984 (WA); a person has a gender history only if they 'identifies as a member of the opposite sex by living, or seeking to live, as a member of the opposite sex'; 'gender reassigned person' is defined through the Gender Reassignment Act 2000 recognition certificate or a BDM registration change - a binary, certificate/medical-anchored formulation; complaint route is the Equal Opportunity Commissioner, 12-month filing limit, exceptions list.

sources.title: Reforms to remove barriers for LGBTQIA+ community | Western Australian Government
sources.claim_summary: WA Cook Labor government media statement (16 April 2024): reforms to remove barriers for the LGBTQIA+ community - trans and gender-diverse Western Australians will no longer be required to undergo medical or surgical reassignment to register a change of sex or gender, via a streamlined administrative process in the Births, Deaths and Marriages registry, implementing Law Reform Commission recommendations (the bill that became the 2024 Act receiving assent 26 September 2024).

sources.title: How to deal with gender discrimination and transphobia (WA) | Justice Connect
sources.claim_summary: JusticeConnect community-legal-centre fact sheet for trans and gender-diverse young people in WA and their families: explains the choice between state (Equal Opportunity Act 'gender history' route) and federal (Sex Discrimination Act gender-identity/cisgender attributes) complaints - a complainant can use one track, not both - evidencing how WA's narrower state definitions push claimants onto federal coverage.
